title: Azure Event Hubs Overview
description: Learn how Event Hubs ingests millions of streaming events per second for real-time analytics.

data.text: Azure Event Hubs is a big data streaming platform and event ingestion service. It can capture, retain, and replay millions of events per second from any source. Unlike Service Bus or Event Grid, Event Hubs is optimized for high-throughput telemetry and analytics scenarios.

terms.definition: A named streaming endpoint that acts as the entry point for events.
An ordered sequence of events within an Event Hub. Partitions allow parallel processing.
An Event Hubs feature that automatically writes event data to Azure Blob Storage or Data Lake.
A purchased capacity unit that provides a specific amount of ingress and egress bandwidth.

data.title: Create an Event Hub Namespace and Hub (Azure CLI)
data.content: Set up a namespace and an Event Hub with 4 partitions:
data.code:
az eventhubs namespace create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --name myEventHubNamespace \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard \
  --capacity 1

az eventhubs eventhub create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --namespace-name myEventHubNamespace \
  --name telemetry \
  --partition-count 4 \
  --message-retention 1

cards.title: Service Bus

data.title: When to Use Event Hubs
data.text: Use Event Hubs when you need to ingest large streams of data from devices or applications and process them in real time. Common use cases include IoT telemetry, application logging, and clickstream analytics.
